Numbers have always felt like the most visible part of storytelling: at the meeting point of shape, timing, and meaning. That curiosity about how people, events, and decisions come together is what drew me to a career as a Data Analyst, and it has grown into a clear commitment to turning raw data into insights that help organisations make smarter, more human-centred decisions. I am originally from Senegal, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my academic and professional journey, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in work that connects evidence, strategy, and measurable impact. What keeps me engaged in this field is the chance to uncover patterns and trends in data quickly and turn them into recommendations that are clear, actionable, and useful for both users and teams.

My academic and professional path has also shaped how I approach complex work. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, learned it within a couple of months, and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those moments because they often begin with a simple question and end with a clear answer. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when deadlines and revisions demanded it.

One of my favourite memories is bringing my family to a company open day, where they began pointing out the data being recorded and asked me to explain it in their own words. Seeing my family connect with the human story behind the numbers confirmed why this profession matters to me. I am now eager to bring this combination of curiosity, structured thinking, and practical problem-solving to a Data Analyst role where I can contribute to meaningful decisions and continue growing through work that helps organisations do more with less.

Clear, truthful reporting matters because it helps communities make sense of the world around them. That belief is what drew me to journalism: a deep curiosity about people, events, and the forces shaping everyday life, together with a belief that accurate, truthful storytelling can make complex issues accessible and meaningful. For me, reporting is a form of public service, informing people clearly and responsibly while bringing forward voices that might otherwise go unheard. This aligns with my interest in turning complex, fast-moving information into stories that are accurate, compelling, and grounded in human context. Therefore, I seek to build on my background through a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, where I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes and strengthened my ability to work through large volumes of information with structure and clarity.

My academic and professional development have been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I moved into an unfamiliar area of work and, within about a quarter, was handling it independently, which showed me how quickly focused learning can translate into reliable delivery. On another project, I developed a new method for a problem my group had treated as unsolvable, and the approach was later adopted by other teams. Colleagues also sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those exchanges because they sharpen my attention to how information is interpreted and used. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to bring it through to completion.

One of my favourite memories is bringing a family member to a local community event I was covering, only for them to recognise someone I planned to interview through an old neighbourhood connection. That moment captured for me why journalism feels so personal and meaningful. It also reflects the way I work with others: when colleagues have asked how I approached a piece or organised a source, I have taken time to walk them through it so they could apply it in their own work. Originally from Brazil, I now want to bring that same sense of care, judgement, and purpose to a journalist role where I can continue learning while producing work that is accurate, credible, and useful to readers.

Few fields reveal the value of intelligent communication as clearly as marketing, where a message can shape what people remember, understand, and respond to. I am now eager to bring this combination of marketing experience, sustained project work, and practical judgement to a Marketing Manager role, contributing thoughtful campaigns, clear communication, and meaningful brand presence.

Originally from Nigeria, I bring a perspective shaped by both academic depth and practical delivery. During a lengthy stretch of work with several setbacks, I stayed with the project through each stage and added extra hours when deadlines demanded it so that progress continued. Looking ahead, I am eager to bring this combination of technical depth, user-focused thinking, and steady follow-through to a Web Developer role where I can continue creating digital experiences that are clear, reliable, and genuinely useful.

Reliable financial information shapes decisions, protects businesses, and helps people rely on them every day. When I was given responsibility in an unfamiliar area of work, I did not handle it independently straight away; over most of a year, I learned the processes step by step until I could manage the work without help. Colleagues also come to me with questions about their own tasks, and I make time to talk them through the steps or clarify what is needed. During one lengthy stretch of work with several setbacks, I stayed with the task through each delay and added extra hours when deadlines required it so that the work could still be completed properly.

What continues to appeal to me about financial accounting is the opportunity to turn complex figures into a financial picture that teams can use with confidence. I am now eager to bring this foundation to a Financial Accountant role where I can contribute dependable reporting, accurate reconciliations, and steady support for the wider financial picture.
